format.name: basin-mask-bitplanes-v1
planes: plane 0 (bytes 0 .. planeBytes-1): 1 = cell is in the basin (HU-2 14 or 15)
plane 1 (bytes planeBytes .. 2*planeBytes-1): 1 = basin cell assigned to HU-2 15 (Lower Colorado); a cell with plane 0 = 1 and plane 1 = 0 is HU-2 14 (Upper Colorado); plane 1 is 0 outside the basin
format.bitOrder: cell index i = y * width + x (row 0 north, as grid.f32); bit i of a plane is (byte[i >> 3] >> (i & 7)) & 1 (least significant bit first)
format.padding: unused high bits of each plane's last byte are 0

description: Mask of the TDA grid (grid.f32) to the U.S. Geological Survey Watershed Boundary Dataset hydrologic regions 14 (Upper Colorado) and 15 (Lower Colorado).

grid.rowOrder: row 0 is north; rows run north to south; cell index i = y * width + x

cellRule: A cell is in the basin when at least half of the native 3″ Copernicus pixels it covers (the same 30 x 30 blocks as grid.f32; 19 px wide in the last column, 18 px tall in the last row) have their centres inside the union of the WBD HU-2 14 and 15 polygons (GDAL rasterization, pixel-centre rule). A basin cell is assigned to whichever of 14 and 15 holds more of its pixels (14 on a tie).

source.datumNote: NAD 83 coordinates are used as WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) without a datum shift. USGS: "All modern maps and GIS data are cast on NAD 83 or WGS 84, which are equivalent datums at map scales of 1:5,000 and smaller." (https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/why-are-nad-83-position-values-so-far-nad-27-values-were-old-coordinates-wrong). The grid is about 1:5,000,000 or smaller on screen and its cells are 0.025°.

coverage: Mexico: the U.S. Watershed Boundary Dataset continues region 15 into Mexico. WBD metadata: areas along the border "have been updated to include harmonized hydrologic units and hydrography that extends across the border", in collaboration with Mexico's INEGI. In the study area this includes the Colorado River's lower course and delta down to the south edge: 1039 basin cells lie mostly in hydrologic units that are entirely in Mexico. The lowest cell of the elevation grid is in one of these units (HU-12 150301080302, whose downstream code in WBD is OCEAN) and is inside the mask.

Gap in Mexico: WBD covers Mexico only as far as its harmonized units go. In the study area, 4 cells in the south-west corner, around 31.87° N, 115.19° W, lie mostly in no WBD unit. They are outside the mask; no boundary has been drawn for them. WBD's Mexican units have not been compared with INEGI's own hydrography.

Region is not drainage: WBD region 15 includes subregion 1508 Sonora. Following WBD's own downstream codes, every one of its 634 smallest units (HU-12) stays inside 1508 and ends at CLOSED BASIN (22), MEXICO (117), OCEAN (495), so none drains to the Colorado. Region 14 includes the Great Divide Closed Basin (HU-6 140402). Both are inside the mask because they are part of WBD regions 14 and 15. Cells: Sonora 1609, Great Divide Closed Basin 1426. Land along the west edge between about 32.5° and 35.1° N is WBD region 18 (California) and is outside the mask.

Study-area edges: parts of both regions lie outside the study rectangle, so the mask covers only the part of each region inside it (for example 48.9% of the Colorado Headwaters and 67.7% of the Upper Green).

Resolution: the mask is per 0.025° cell (about 2.2 km x 2.8 km); 1840 cells straddle the basin boundary and count as basin when at least half of their elevation pixels fall inside it. WBD metadata: "At a minimum, the HUs are delineated at 1:24,000-scale in the conterminous United States".

mexicoOnlyHu12.rule: basin cells with at least half their pixels in WBD HU-12 units whose states attribute is exactly 'MX' (a lower bound: HU-12s shared with a U.S. state are not counted)

sonoraDrainage.rule: for every HU-12 in HU-4 1508, follow WBD's tohuc (downstream HU-12) until a code that is not an HU-12 of regions 14/15; count those terminal codes

reproducible: No timestamps; the same cached WBD zips and grid give the same bytes. accessDate is the date the zip was downloaded (from the cache sidecar).
